findings.problem: The about said acceptPayoutQuoteInTx 'binds the Payment to the quote'. It does not: it sends the door event send_claimed when the execution takes its submission claim. The real binding is bindPayoutPaymentInTx (event payment_bound), which the payments birth write calls, and the record left that path out completely.
The about left out that the door sends nothing for a refused line (no `to`). The `was` cited only import lines, not the four call sites or the door's write.

'initiated ... once per Payment' was wrong. The claim belongs to the command (paymentCommands.paymentInitiatedClaimedAt), and the SDK then sends one event per Payment item. The backend claims only when the execution has not succeeded, and on the build path only for a request with items. A request checkout never sends it. The claim is used up even when the client never sends the event.

The record left out an idempotency fact. Scheduling the event patches the Payment row: it bumps lifecycleSequence, which becomes causal_sequence, and on a terminal it sets terminalOutcome, terminalEventId and terminalAt. A second terminal for the same Payment is then skipped, except for a rail return after settled. The writer also schedules one job per Payment, falling back to every Payment of the command.
The `was` listed only 5 of the 18 backend producers. All 13 sites that send `progressed` were missing.

The actor mapping cited only the ADR. The old code has its own who-acts table, WHO_ACTS in the generated error pages, which confirms the mapping and documents the catch-all codes as by-mode. Added both citations.

The old code documents these four codes as class `by-mode`. The book's ErrorSpec.class has no by-mode value, so each is booked with its no-mode class, `defect` (actor operator). That is accurate for the no-mode case only. It cannot be fixed inside this file.

designFindings: Exit codes are written twice. exitClass and the CLI_CODE_EXITS table (catalog.ts:21 says 'as the commands that raise it write it') sit beside a hand-written exitCode at every CliFailure raise site, and the two disagree: payment cancel's WRONG_STATE exits 5 (commands/payment/internal/voids.ts:22) while exitClass says 2 (runtime/errors.ts:222).

The protocol has no per-code retryable fact, and three predicates disagree. The SDK's identity isRetryable counts UNKNOWN and NETWORK_ERROR as retryable (packages/sdk/src/access/identity/model.ts:58-67). The CLI offers a retry only for the provider-unavailable class and says UNKNOWN 'offers no retry' (apps/cli/src/runtime/outcome-message.ts:10-18). The ChainCause carries its own retryable flag (protocol/src/errors/schema.ts:23).

The code does not settle 'who acts' for the four catch-all codes (PROVIDER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, TRANSACTION_FAILED, EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED). The class comes from the mode at runtime (classes.ts:70-73,114-121), and the docs print 'Depends on the error's mode' (error-pages.ts:20). Who acts is never stored; it exists only as ADR prose and a docs string table (error-pages.ts:13-21).

CLI-only codes live outside the protocol code list (CliErrorCode, runtime/errors.ts:29-41). Their class table is in one file (errors.ts:68-79) and their exit table in another (commands/schema/catalog.ts:22-30).

13 of the 16 concept error tables are empty boilerplate, including payments' own (protocol/src/payments/error-codes.ts:6-11). Payments refusals are generic codes with reason strings instead, for example EVIDENCE_MISMATCH in payments/verifications/writes/claims.ts:55.

Telemetry plumbing mutates domain rows. Scheduling payment_transitioned patches the Payment's lifecycleSequence, terminalOutcome, terminalEventId and terminalAt (payments/events/writer.ts:217-222), so the event's causal sequence and terminal dedupe are stored on the Payment row. payment_verification_retry goes through the same writer and bumps every Payment's lifecycleSequence (writer.ts:93-117).

payment_initiated has split ownership. The backend spends a durable one-shot claim (commands/writes/initiations.ts:20-21), but the event is sent fire and forget by the client and only if a telemetry port is set (sdk/src/payments/events.ts:19-34). A lost emit is never re-sent, and request checkouts never send it (sdk/src/requests/checkout-payments.ts:166,232).
Telemetry hard-codes the chain id to Base Sepolia (payments/verifications/events.ts:33; events/writer.ts:228 default).

Producers send props the catalog schemas do not declare: pool_cause on payment_verification_retry and failed payment_transitioned (verifications/events.ts:36; deliveries.ts:136,187), while the catalog structs omit it (observability/src/events/money.ts:142-187).

Legacy event names are still accepted by the delivery validator (payments/events/deliveries.ts:34-38). The retired deposit events stay in the payments catalog (catalog/schemas.ts:53; catalog/domains/payments.ts:20-21). Orphan doc comments for deleted deposit_settled operations remain in observability/src/operations/indexing.ts:18-19.

Payments deep-imports other concepts' internals instead of their doors. It reaches into #banking/payouts/writes/payments, reads, refunds and events, although banking/index.ts:15-18 exports the same functions. It also reaches into #payroll/runs/writes/progression and #requests/writes/approvals. Payments mutations therefore write the payouts, payrollRuns and request rows, and schedule payout_transitioned, payroll_run_transitioned and invoice_request_transitioned inside payments transactions.

quick_pay_external_address_acknowledged requires a raw recipient_address (observability/src/events/money.ts:193), and RecipientTelemetryProps carries recipient_address too (money.ts:120). The money domain's own rule says 'No raw emails or raw addresses' (money.ts:26).

The `kind` property of payment_transitioned has two vocabularies for an unspecified purpose. The SDK's initiated maps it to 'quick_pay' (sdk/src/payments/prepared-execution.ts:71), but the backend's failed sends 'unspecified' (backend/src/payments/writes/outcomes.ts:114).

payment_writer_incident is called an event but is a console.error JSON line (payments/events/writer.ts:35-48), outside the catalog and PostHog. It is the only signal for 11 incident sites in deposits, rollbacks, conflicts and finishes.
result.notes:
I fixed vocabulary.ts in place. It typechecks cleanly: `npx tsc -p .` prints no lines for vocabulary.ts. It loads at runtime with 59 records: 50 errors and 9 events. That is the original 57 plus event_payroll_run_transitioned and event_invoice_request_transitioned, both labelled additions in the same way as payout_transitioned.

I re-checked every error record against the old code, and these all hold:
- **Codes:** the 32 platform codes (codes.ts:27-61), 4 from organizations, 6 from payroll and 1 from permissions are all present. The other 13 concept tables are empty.
- **Class:** every class matches CODE_CLASSES, the concept tables or CLI_CODE_CLASSES.
- **Exit:** every exit matches exitClass, REFUSED_INPUT_OR_STATE, EXPECTED_OPERATION_OUTCOMES or CLI_CODE_EXITS. I walked all 50 by hand.
- **Message:** every message is the copy's summary word for word, and every copy line citation is correct.
- **Event props:** they match the catalog schemas (money.ts, banking.ts, envelope.ts, values.ts).
- **Line ranges:** the header ranges check out (classes.ts, codes.ts, errors.ts, catalog.ts, model.ts, failure-modes.ts).
- **Retryable** stays a documented judgement call.

The two new events are not yet in any sibling's `emits`. The verifications, commands and movements writers may want to add them:
- event_payroll_run_transitioned: the submission write, and the settle paths in claims, sends, commitments and settlements.
- event_invoice_request_transitioned: the request-prepare write in payments/commands/writes/requests.ts.

executions.ts already imports event_payout_transitioned. No sibling records are missing.
